candidate_name: National LNG regasification plant (Proinversion tender, no site or bidder named)
sponsor_or_proposer: Government of Peru / Ministerio de Energia y Minas (MINEM) -- to be tendered via Proinversion; no company/consortium named yet
current_state: On 16 Mar 2026 Energy Minister Angelo Alfaro announced the government will commission Proinversion to launch a public tender for a new LNG regasification plant, targeting roughly a two-year build once launched. The stated rationale is energy security / avoiding natural-gas supply contingencies, not a specific port or region. The article explicitly distinguishes this from Peru's existing 14 small regasification STATIONS (6 in the southwest concession, 8 in the north), which redistribute LNG trucked domestically rather than importing it; this new plant is described as importing LNG directly via LNG carriers ('buques metaneros') and connecting it to the pipeline network -- i.e. it would be Peru's first dedicated marine-import LNG terminal apart from the already-cancelled Ilo LNG Terminal (T100000130990, unrelated bi-national Peru-Bolivia pipeline concept). A follow-up targeted search found no later 2026 reporting naming a location, sponsor, or bidder.
missing_threshold_elements: Sponsor: none named (pre-tender, government intent only). Location: none named (no port/region specified). Concrete step: partially present (ministerial commissioning of Proinversion to launch a tender is more than pure verbal intent, but no tender has yet been launched and no bidder selected).
watch_for: Proinversion tender launch notice; any port/region named (Ilo/southern concession vs. a north-coast site vs. Callao/Lima area); a winning bidder or sponsor consortium.
